WESTMEATH COUNTY COUNCIL Local Authority Development - File Ref. LAA1 2026  
 
Active Travel Scheme Cornamaddy to Garrycastle (Route F) Athlone 
Nature and extent of the proposed Development: 
This subject proposal is for Route F (2.3km) in length and commences from Cornamaddy 
Roundabout to Wash House Turn Roundabout (R916). The scheme is located on the eastern 
side of Athlone and extends from north of the national road N55 to south along the regional 
road R916. 
• 
The provision of a 2.2m wide one-way segregated cycle track both sides of the 
carriageway, reducing in places where constraints exist. 
• 
The provision of 2.0m wide footpaths on both sides of the carriageway, reducing in 
places where constraints exist. 
• 
Vehicular carriageway width of 6m, minimum width of 3m per lane. 
• 
Junction realignments and the introduction of raised crossings on all side roads. 
• 
Straight through cycle lane/track crossings on side road junctions. 
• 
The provision of signalised crossings for pedestrians and cyclists. 
• 
Upgrading of the Garrycastle Roundabout and Altown Roundabout to roundabouts 
with provisions for pedestrians and cyclists. 
• 
The provision of landscaping along the route. 
This report has been prepared in accordance with Section 179 of the Planning and 
Development Act 2000 (as amended) and Part 8 of the Planning and Development Regulations 
2001 (as amended).

Project Background 
Westmeath County Council (WCC) is progressing improvements to cycling and pedestrian 
infrastructure along a series of roads within Athlone, Co. Westmeath, comprising 
approximately 15 kilometres of active travel routes. The submitted documentation states that 
these works have been subdivided into six individual sub-routes, each at varying stages of 
design and development, as illustrated in Figure 1 below. 
 
Figure 1 Location of proposed Active Travel routes in Athlone currently being designed – Route F highlighted in Red 
The subject Part 8 application relates specifically to Route F (indicated green) and outlined in 
red, which is described as commencing from the Cornamaddy Roundabout extending south 
to Wash House Turn Roundabout (R916). The proposed development comprises the provision 
of cycleway and footpath infrastructure over a length of approximately 2.3 kilometres. 
The documentation further indicates that the purpose of the scheme is to enhance safety, 
connectivity, and accessibility for pedestrians and cyclists, in support of a modal shift towards 
more sustainable transport modes and improved integration with the wider active travel 
network in Athlone.

1.5 
Description and extent of the development proposed 
The proposed scheme will provide segregated one-way cycle tracks on both sides of the road, 
or two-way cycle tracks along the north side of the road, together with standard footpaths. 
Localised sections of shared active travel paths are required due to constrained widths at 
several of the roundabouts. Key features of the scheme are outlined by chainage sections 
below. 
Chainage 0+050 to 0+350 Segment F4 at TUS: 
It is proposed to construct a standard one-way cycle track (min. 1.7m) along with segregated 
footpath (min. 1.8m) on both sides of the carriageway. All minor side-road junctions will be 
provided with a raised table uncontrolled crossings with stop lines pulled back in advance of 
the raised tables. 
An existing signalised crossing will be upgraded to raised signalised crossing at chainage 
0+075m and a new raised signalised pedestrian crossing will be proposed at chainage 
0+260m. Three minor side-road junctions will be upgraded at chainage 0+140m, 0+155m and 
0+225m with raised table uncontrolled crossings. 
Some sections of land acquisition is required for segregated cycle track and footpath from 
chainage 0+170 to 0+300 & 0+325 to 0+345 along the eastern side along the carriageway.

Chainage 0+350 to 0+450 Garrycastle Roundabout: 
The existing Garrycastle roundabout will be modiﬁed to a Segregated Roundabout with 
Shared Active Travel Facilities, however it will be retaining the majority of features. No 
changes will be proposed to the central island. Raised table crossings will be provided on 
each arm with the following details: 
• All arms of the roundabout will provide raised table combined zebra crossings 4.0m 
in width, to cater for both cyclist and pedestrian movements. 
• The double entry vehicular lanes along northern and southern arms of the 
roundabout will be reduced to single lane entry only. 
• Traﬃc island on all the arms will be replaced with ghost island and raised table crossing 
facilities. 
The modiﬁed Garrycastle Roundabout will be connected to a standard one-way cycle track on 
the southern arm and will join the existing one-way cycle facility on the northern arm while 
shared facilities are proposed throughout the roundabout surrounds.  
 
Chainage 0+450 to 0+880 Segment F3: 
It is proposed to retain the existing footpaths and one way cycle facilities in both directions 
throughout this segment and this location will be further monitored by the Council. If the 
cycle/pedestrian traﬃc increases over the years it is at that point the cycle track/footpath 
widths will be reassessed and redesigned as required for active travel uptake. The existing 
carriageway width will be reduced to min. 6.0m per running lane and speed reduction 
measures in the form of raised tables will be provided at chainage 0+550m and 0+725m. 
As most of the segment will be retained and with rapid build proposals, land acquisition will 
not be required along the segment. 
 
Chainage 0+850 to 0+950 Junction F1 (Altown Roundabout). 
The general layout of the roundabout itself will be retained with improvements for 
pedestrians and cyclists proposed for the surrounding area. These improvements will come 
in the form of raised table crossings on each arm with the following details: 
• All arms of the roundabout will provide raised table combined zebra crossing of 4.0m 
wide to cater both cycle and pedestrian movement. 
• The double entry vehicular lanes along northern and southern arm of the 
roundabout will be reduced to single entry only.

• The traﬃc islands on all the arms will be replaced with ghost island road markings 
and raised table crossing facilities. 
The modiﬁed Altown Roundabout will be connected to the existing one-way cycle track at the 
south-eastern arm (IDA Business & Technology Park) and will join the two-way cycle facility 
on the north-western arm (Cartrontroy) while shared facilities will be proposed in between 
the raised crossings. 
 
Chainage 0+950 to 1+320 Segment F2. 
It is proposed to retain the existing footpaths and two-way cycle facilities throughout this 
segment and this location will be further monitored by the Council. If the cycle/pedestrian 
traﬃc increases over the years it is at that point the cycle track/footpath widths will be 
reassessed and redesigned as required for active travel uptake. 
The existing carriageway which is 4 lanes mostly, is unchanged mostly along this segment 
while carriageway width has been reduced to min. 6.0m from chainage 0+950m to 1+150m. 
The two-way cycle track facility and footpath will be swapped from chainage 0+950 to 
0+975m. New bus stop locations will be proposed at chainage 0+975 for southbound 
commuters and 1+000 for northbound commuters. Side road junction crossing facilities will 
be upgraded with new tactile paving and shared path facilities as per CDM (Cycle Design 
Manual). 
This segment is crossing the N6 Motorway with an overbridge from chainage 1+150m to 
1+250m. After Chainage 1+150m, the existing cross-section has been retained mostly while 
upgrading only the side riad crossing facilities. 
As most of the segment will be retained and with rapid build proposals, land acquisition will 
not be required along the segment. 
 
Chainage 1+320 to 2+250 Part of Segment F1 
The whole length of the cross-section has been proposed as a standard one-way cycle track 
(min. 1.7m) along with segregated footpath (min. 1.8m) on both side of the carriageway. All 
minor side-road junctions will be provided with a raised table uncontrolled crossing with 
stop lines pulled back in advance of the raised tables, except at Woodville Avenue Junction 
and Blyry Court Junction, where a 5m dwell area will be provided for one vehicle as per 
TL401 of the CDM. 
This segment comprises of the following details:

• Moydrum Road Junction radii (1+320 to 1+350) will be tightened and the existing 
two-way cycle facility will be connected to the new two-way cycle facility on the 
northern side of the junction. A signalised crossing will allow cyclists to diverge from 
the two-way cycle track to a one-way cycle track on both side of the road. A 
retaining structure will be required in the northeast corner, and will be detailed in 
the detail design stage, adjacent to the Steeltech Sheds boundary due to the level 
diﬀerences at this location. 
• From chainage 1+350 to 2+250, the Segment will continue with the new standard 
one-way cycle tracks on both sides of the carriageway with all side road junctions 
and private access/entrances to be upgraded with a raised table uncontrolled 
crossing with stop lines pulled back in advance of the raised tables. The ghost island 
and left turn pockets will be removed to accommodate the new oﬀ-road cycle track 
facility, while the existing carriageway width will be reduced to 6.0m kerb to kerb. 
• The existing signalised crossing facility on chainage 1+560 will be upgraded to a 
raised signalised crossing while three new raised signalised crossing facilities are 
proposed at chainage 1+770, 1+970 and 2+160 as per TL 607 of the CDM. 
• The existing bus stops near Ericssons for both northbound and southbound 
commuters will be upgraded at chainage 1+600, 1+640 as per TL203 of the CDM. 
• The existing bus stops near the Cornamaddy National School will be upgraded to 
shared bus stop facilities at chainage 2+050, 2+060 for both northbound and 
southbound traﬃc as per TL202 of the CDM. 
It is not envisaged that land take will be required within this segment as all proposals can be 
incorporated within the existing road corridor. 
 
Identified benefits and improvements: 
Pedestrian Improvements: The new facilities will provide safe, accessible and attractive 
routes for all pedestrians, with a minimum 1.8m wide footpath to be provided in all areas. 
The proposed footpath and cycle link improvements adjacent to the Cornamaddy National 
school may improve cycling take up by students, while also providing safer crossing facilities, 
as outlined within the Preliminary Design Drawings in Appendix A. The location of these 
crossings will improve access and permeability for pedestrians to the residential, recreational 
and retail areas within the scheme extents; and onwards to the commercial, educational and 
transport hubs closer to the town centre. Facilities for those users with visual or mobility 
impairments will be much improved, with tactile paving, flush kerbs and raised crossings 
provided throughout. 
Cyclists: 
The provision of improved cycling facilities throughout this route will be 
beneficial to cyclists using R916 to travel to TUS, Cornamaddy National School, places of work,

and other key locations within Athlone. The provision of high-quality cycle infrastructure will 
provide attractive and safe routes for cyclists linking many residential, educational and 
commercial areas, as well as connections to other proposed cycleways in the area. 
Vehicular Traffic: 
There will be some impacts to the existing vehicular traffic on the 
surrounding road network, particularly during the construction phases. Given the nature of 
the proposals (e.g., reduction in carriageway width, reduction in junction radii and an increase 
in pedestrian/cyclist crossings) there will be a slowing of vehicular speeds compared to that 
existing. 
There are no design layout changes proposed to the junction connecting to N6 Motorway; 
however it is proposed to reduce dual lane entry and exits on all roundabouts to single lane 
entry and exits. These upgrades will bring all roundabouts in-line with the current standards 
(i.e. DMURS and the Cycle Design Manual). As a knock-on impact of the lane reduction, this 
may result in a reduction in vehicle capacity of the roundabouts. In addition the proposed 
decrease of junction kerb radii, removal of some left-turn slips, and the provision of 
pedestrian and cyclist crossings on all arms of a junctions may also impact vehicular capacity. 
It is envisaged these vehicle impacts will be minimal. 
These junction improvements and lane reductions are necessary in order to provide a scheme 
which is safe and in line with best practice and guidelines. These proposals will help to reduce 
the likelihood of conflicts between all road users. The improvements to pedestrian and cycling 
infrastructure will encourage a modal shift away from the private vehicle, which should have 
a corresponding effect on reducing traffic volumes locally.

1.7 Policy Context  
1.7.1 National & Regional Policy Context 
Project Ireland 2040 - Revised National Planning Framework – April 2025 (NPF) 
The National Planning Framework (NPF) emphasises the importance of reducing reliance on 
private cars by promoting the development of high-quality walking and cycling infrastructure. 
This approach aims to support healthier, more active lifestyles and to foster more sustainable, 
accessible, and liveable urban environments. 
National Policy Objective 37: requires the integration of safe, convenient, and attractive 
alternatives to car travel into the design of communities. It specifically prioritises walking and 
cycling access in both new and existing developments, ensuring that active travel is a viable 
and appealing option for people of all ages. 
National Policy Objective 93: reinforces this by promoting integrated spatial planning that 
supports walking and cycling as preferred modes of transport. The objective links active travel 
infrastructure with broader goals of improving air quality and reducing exposure to pollution, 
recognising the role of walking and cycling in creating healthier and more environmentally 
sustainable communities. 
Project Ireland 2040 - National Development Plan (NDP) 
The NDP emphasises the need to provide “safe alternative active travel options such as 
segregated cycling and walking facilities can also help alleviate congestion and meet climate 
action objectives by providing viable alternatives and connectivity with existing public 
transport infrastructure”. The NDP encourages a significant “modal shift through greater 
levels of investment and further development of meaningful alternatives to private car uses, 
such as new urban cycling and walking routes which will provide additional sustainable travel 
options.” 
Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy for the Eastern and Midland Region (RSES) (2019-
2031)  
The RSES promotes healthy placemaking and recognises the importance of active travel 
measures to bring about behavioural changes and more sustainable transport use. In this 
regard, it is recognised that the provision of cycleways can enhance areas, contributing to 
more attractive places and create opportunities to be physically active and reduce the 
negative consequences of car-based commuting.

It is a Regional Policy Objective that Local authorities seek to support the planned provision 
of easily accessible social, community, cultural and recreational facilities and ensure that all 
communities have access to a range of facilities that meet the needs of the communities they 
serve (RPO 9.14). 
 
Climate Action Plan 2025 
The Climate Action Plan supports the transition to a net zero carbon society and promotes 
sustainable travel through expanded walking, cycling, and public transport infrastructure. 
Relevant measures include Action TR/25/7, which commits to advancing the rollout of walking 
and cycling infrastructure in line with the National Cycle Network and Cycle Connects plans. 
 
1.7.2 Local Policy Context 
Westmeath County Development Plan 2021-2027 (WCDP) 
The proposed active travel scheme in Athlone directly supports the overarching aim of the 
Westmeath County Development Plan to achieve a sustainable, integrated, and low-carbon 
transport system with excellent connectivity by enhancing existing transport infrastructure to 
facilitate safer and more convenient active travel. 
Specifically: 
• 
Integration of land use and transport (CPO 2.16): The proposal prioritises cycling and 
walking through segregated cycle tracks, footpaths, and shared crossings, promoting 
active travel as a viable mode of transport alongside public transport. 
• 
Promotion of sustainable transport and walkable communities (CPO 7.3 & CPO 10.2): 
By providing safe, accessible, and direct routes for pedestrians and cyclists, the 
scheme encourages modal shift away from private cars, making everyday facilities 
and services within short walking or cycling distances. 
• 
Enhanced transport connectivity (CPO 10.1 & CPO 10.12): The project improves 
access to bus stops, key junctions, and transport interchanges, supporting multi-
modal travel and providing facilities such as cycle connections to public transport. 
• 
Health, safety, and environmental benefits (CPO 10.11 & CPO 10.15): The 
development includes safe, direct, and convenient cycle routes and footpaths, with 
physical separation from vehicular traffic, enhancing the streetscape for pedestrians, 
cyclists, and people with reduced mobility.

Design standards and best practice (CPO 10.13): All cycle and pedestrian 
infrastructure is proposed in line with the National Cycle Manual, the Design Manual 
for Urban Roads and Streets, and international best practice, ensuring high-quality, 
future-proof active travel provision. 
 
Athlone Town Development Plan 2014-2020 (ATDP) 
It is Council policy to develop walking and cycling routes in Athlone (policies P-TR2, P-WC1, P-
WC2), to provide a network of on-road and greenway pedestrian and cycle routes within the 
town (O-WC14), secure vibrant streets that are permeable and well connected with 
appropriate pedestrian and cycle infrastructure (P-TM7) and improve existing streets in terms 
of pedestrians and cyclists inter-alia (O-TM12). 
 
1.8  
Ecology 
The proposed works are not located within any designated pNHA, NHA, SAC or SPA. It is 
Council policy ‘to protect, manage and enhance the natural heritage, biodiversity, landscape 
and environment of Athlone, in recognition of its importance as a non-renewable resource, 
unique identifier and as a natural resource asset’ (P-NH1) and ‘ require Appropriate 
Assessment (Habitats Directive Assessment) and where relevant environmental assessment 
such as EIA (Environmental Impact Assessment), or Ecological Appraisal for developments not 
directly connected with or necessary to the management of a European site, and which are 
likely to have significant effects on the integrity of the site individually or cumulatively’ (P-
NH10)  
The nearest European sites are the Crosswood Bog SAC (002337), Lough Ree SAC (000440), 
Lough Ree SPA (004064) River Shannon Callows SAC (site code:000216) and Middle Shannon 
Callow SPA (site code:000216) all located within 2.5km of the development site. Of these 
sites, it is noted that River Shannon Callows SAC (site code:000216) and Middle Shannon 
Callow SPA (site code:000216) are located downstream of the development and as such no 
significant impacts are anticipated from the development.

1.10  Services Provision 
 
No water and foul water connections are required as part of this development. 
 
1.11  Infrastructure Design & Effective Assimilation into its Surroundings 
The proposed scheme has been designed in accordance with the Design Manual for Urban 
Roads and Streets (DMURS) and the Cycle Design Manual (CDM), ensuring appropriate cycle 
and pedestrian widths and integration with the surrounding environment. 
 
1.12  Road Safety & Sustainable Travel 
The scheme prioritises road safety and sustainable travel in line with DMURS (2019) and the 
CDM. No road safety issues have been identified in relation to this Part 8 proposal. 
 
1.13  Appropriate Assessment 
Appropriate Assessment is a standard legal requirement for all plans and projects likely to 
have a significant impact on European sites i.e. Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) or Special 
Protection Areas (SPA). The subject lands are not designated within a European Site.  
The nearest European sites are the Crosswood Bog SAC (002337), Lough Ree SAC (000440), 
Lough Ree SPA (004064) River Shannon Callows SAC (site code:000216) and Middle Shannon 
Callow SPA (site code:000216) all located within 2.5km of the development site. Of these 
sites, it is noted that River Shannon Callows SAC (site code:000216) and Middle Shannon 
Callow SPA (site code:000216) are located downstream of the development. 
The proposed scheme has undergone an Appropriate Assessment screening in accordance 
with Article 6(3) of the Habitats Directive. Having considered the contents of the Screening 
for Appropriate Assessment report, together with the nature, type, scale and location of the 
of the proposed works within a built-up urban area, it is considered that the proposed 
development, individually or in combination with another project, will not give rise to 
significant adverse direct, indirect or secondary impacts on the integrity of any Natura 2000 
sites, having regard to their conservation objectives. It is therefore concluded that 
progression to the second stage, a full Appropriate Assessment and accompanying Natura 
Impact Statement is not required in this instance.

1.14  Environmental Impact Assessment  
The proposed development does not fall within the mandatory requirement for an EIA as 
addressed in EU Directive 85/337/EEC (as amended by Directive 97/11/EC).  
An Environmental Impact Assessment Screening exercise was undertaken as part of the pre-
assessment determination. The screening report determined there is no real likelihood of 
significant effects on the environment arising from the proposed development and concluded 
that an Environmental Impact Assessment was not required in this instance. 
Having regard to the information presented for the development in the plan proposals, it is 
reasonable to conclude that there is no real likelihood of significant effects on the 
environment arising from the proposed development and a full Environmental Impact 
Assessment is not required.

2.0 Internal Section Reports and Prescribed Bodies Submissions 
2.1 Internal Sections Reports Received 
Environment Section 
Report received on 23 June 2026.  The report advises that they have reviewed the AA 
Screening Assessment completed by Atkins-Réalis, which concluded that this development 
has been screened out from proceeding to a Stage 2 AA Report. The Environment Section 
concur with this conclusion and the Determination report by the Planning Authority. 
The report confirms no objection is raised, subject to the prior submission and written 
agreement of the Planning Authority for a Construction Environmental Management Plan 
(CEMP) and a Construction and Demolition Resource Waste Management Plan (RWMP). In 
respect of surface water attenuation, the report suggests that it would be desirable that 
where feasible, nature-based solutions be incorporated into this design element. 
Matters concerning the provision of a standard construction measures, including bunded 
store for oils and hydrocarbons, the implementation of dust controls with agreed monitoring 
locations, and adherence to construction noise limits are typically addressed within the CEMP. 
 
Westmeath National Road Office 
WNRO has evaluated this application and considers that this application has no impact on any 
proposed schemes and therefore has no objections or observations regarding the proposed 
development.

2.2 Prescribed Bodies Reports Received 
Uisce Éireann 
Report received 16th June 2026. Uisce Éireann has no objection in principle to the proposal. 
The report identifies that records indicate the presence of multiple water services 
infrastructure which may be impacted by the proposed development. Therefore, UÉ requests 
the applicant to liaise with UÉ during the final design stage of the proposed development 
works, in order to ascertain the potential impacts on the existing Uisce Éireann network 
infrastructure, in order for protection works or replacement works can be agreed and carried 
out as appropriate.  
UÉ requests that prior to any works being undertaken, that the location of any / all 
watermain(s) / sewer(s) and any associated fittings shall be confirmed on the ground with the 
local water curator.  
It is further stated that the new kerb-lines should be set out on site so that the local water 
curator can ensure that the new kerb-line will not be sitting on top of the existing water main 
and/or sewer line, as the new kerb-lines maybe in close proximity to this infrastructure in the 
submitted drawings. UÉ requests that the integrity of the infrastructure shall be protected 
during the works and the Council's water service's engineer consulted prior to and during 
construction. 
TII 
Report received on 15/06/2026. TII requests that the planning authority has regard to the 
provisions of Chapter 3 of the DoECLG Spatial Planning and National Roads Guidelines in the 
assessment and determination of the subject application. 
TII notes that the proposed route travels along the R916 which crosses the N6 on a TII 
Structure (Eirspan Name: Garrankesh Overbridge, Eirspan ID:WH-N06-006). This bridge is dual 
span with a physically separated dedicated pedestrian/ cycle track. General Arrangement 
Drawing Nos.2 and 3 of 4 (Dwg. Nos.0086381-ATK-F1-01-DR-CE-900 and 0086381-ATK-F1-01-
DR-CE-90010, Rev C01) indicate this existing active travel infrastructure will be retained in the 
scheme.  TII however notes that both drawings include annotations and text as follows; 
“bollards to be removed as they will become potential hazard for the users”.  In the interests 
of clarity, TII highlights that existing concrete bollards at either end of the dedicated 
pedestrian/ cycle overbridge have been installed in the interests of traffic and road user safety 
generally to discourage drivers from entering the dedicated cycle overbridge in error.  As such, 
the existing concrete bollards at either end of the dedicated cycle bridge are recommended 
to also be retained in the proposed scheme.

The Irish Cycling Campaign (formerly Cyclist.ie, the Irish Cycling Advocacy Network-ICAN), is 
the national advocacy body for cycling in Ireland with Local Groups operating on a 
countrywide basis. It is the Irish member of the European Cyclists’ Federation and a member 
of the Irish Environmental Network. 
While broadly welcoming any proposed improvements in cycling and walking infrastructure 
that help to make the public realm safer for all, the Irish Cycling Campaign (ICC) is very 
disappointed with the “hodge podge approach and very mixed standards of design” proposed 
for this active travel upgrade of the Garrycastle to Cornamaddy Roundabout over a distance 
of 2.25km. 
 
2.1 General Comments - Mixed Quality Standards: 
The scheme demonstrates inconsistent design standards along the 2 km stretch, with many 
elements falling below the Cycle Design Manual (CDM) recommendations, particularly in 
relation to widths. There is also a lack of consistency in roundabout design, with a mix of 
segregated and shared pedestrian–cycle facilities rather than a uniform approach. 
 
Response – The scheme proposes to maximise the use of existing cycle infrastructure including 
some resurfacing of cycle infrastructure to meet current standards, where required. All 
roundabouts are consistent designs utilising shared space in line with the Cycle Design 
Manual. 
 
2.2 CH 0+00 to Garrycastle Roundabout 
The R446 roundabout upgrade is a positive improvement, particularly with the introduction 
of protected crossings, though there is a lack of clarity on crossing design and a need for 
consistency across all arms. Concerns remain around the use of shared pedestrian–cycle 
facilities and substandard cycle track widths (1.7 m vs 2.0 m recommended), despite sufficient 
space being available for segregation. 
Further along the route, enhancements such as signalised crossings, raised junctions, and 
reduced carriageway widths are welcomed, although constrained cycle track widths are only 
partially justified. The Garrycastle Roundabout is a key concern, as it has not been redesigned 
to include segregated facilities despite ample space, and it is recommended that this be 
revisited in line with best practice. 
Response – The proposed roundabout designs are in line with the CDM TL703 segregated 
Roundabout with Shared Active Travel Facilities. As outlined within the Cycle Design Manual 
TL703 Note 2) Other protected roundabout layouts (TL 701 or TL 702) are preferred, where 
space permits. The proposals within this section from CH0 to the Garrycastle Roundabout 
conform to the CDM with segregated one-way cycle facilities proposed.  Increased cycle track 
widths would require additional land acquisition outside the existing road corridor.

2.3 CH 0+450 to CH 0+950 
This section highlights a lack of meaningful upgrades along a constrained part of the route, 
with the adoption of a “wait and see” approach considered inappropriate given the existing 
substandard 1.3 m cycle track. While traffic calming measures such as speed ramps are 
proposed, the absence of immediate improvements to cycling infrastructure is a key concern. 
At the Greenway/Altown Roundabout, although safety measures like zebra crossings and

3 Summary/ Conclusion 
Overall the Irish Cycling Campaign is disappointed with the approach taken including use of a 
confused mix of designs for the overall improvement of this Route F between Cornamaddy 
roundabout and the R446 roundabout over a distance of 2.25km. While welcoming the overall 
improvement in pedestrian and cyclist crossing links along the proposed scheme, and the 
tightening of junction approaches, we are critical of the lack of consistency in the approach 
to the overall route F3: 
●There are too many shared pedestrian/cyclist sections proposed at a number of 
roundabouts, while segregated facilities are provided at one? 
●The proposed cycle track widths are consistently below CDM desirable minimum 
widths. 
●The proposed cycle track switches between 2-way and 1-way systems to the 
confusion and inconvenience of travelling cyclists. 
●The ‘do-nothing’ approach to significant sections of this F3 route compromises the 
overall validity of the proposals.  
The Irish Cycling Campaign would hope that a more consistent and CDM aligned design 
approach is taken to this proposed scheme and urges that the Council reconsider the overall 
design approach, and the adaption of acceptable standards. 
 
Response – The cycle track widths are within the standard allowance for absolute min, due to 
space constraints. 
The proposed design alternates between two-way and one-way cycle tracks for several 
reasons, including the need to retain the existing combined pedestrian and cyclist two-way 
overbridge crossing the N6, as well as local space constraints.

combined pedestrian and cyclist two-way overbridge crossing the N6, as well as local space
